clue.text: Name for a pet (female) in the Orient

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet
her is the female pronoun
taken as written
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a name for their female pet in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine is a girl's given name, so the answer is an example of a name.

clue.text: Firm-faced — but the body's heavenly

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to have faced an opponent is to have met them

explanation.surface: A stern-looking person who nonetheless has a divine figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'the body is heavenly', i.e. a heavenly body; 'Firm-faced' looks like one word but splits into firm and faced.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an astronomical object, one kind of heavenly body.

clue.text: There's point about displeasure when fruit is served

indicators.note: one piece goes round, about, the other here

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork
anger is strong displeasure

explanation.surface: A diner shows annoyance when the fruit course arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: It is a Monet newly discovered, that's the judgement

indicators.note: something newly found is presented in a fresh form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An art expert pronounces a freshly found painting to be by Monet.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimation is an assessment or opinion formed, a judgement.

clue.text: Halt! Road up. Flow one way

definitions.text: Halt! Road up. Flow one way

parts.words: Halt! Road up. Flow one way
parts.note: read like a string of traffic signs, the clue describes a road that is blocked so movement can go no further, a dead end or deadlock

explanation.surface: A set of roadwork signs telling drivers to stop and follow one-way flow.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a blind alley or a deadlock where no progress is possible, just as traffic halts at a closed road.

clue.text: Rubbish to look at and flush

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
to flush something out is to wash it

explanation.surface: Instructions for inspecting then rinsing a sore eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for nonsense or humbug, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: School head requiring high hedge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: something high is tall

explanation.surface: A headteacher who insists on a tall hedge round the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedge' looks like a garden noun, but here it is the verb meaning to avoid committing oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time or prevaricate, which is what hedging means as a verb.

clue.text: Killed in a tussle with the enemy

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the words that follow, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: A soldier's fate in hand-to-hand fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew is the past tense of slay, meaning put to death.

clue.text: A fellow advocate

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A man who acts as a supporter of some cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of another person, as an advocate does.

clue.text: Scholarly folk given titles are bewildered

indicators.note: bewildered means confused and mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Academics confused by honours bestowed on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Literates are educated, learned people, which is what scholarly folk are.

clue.text: Married — a trap for an artist

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: Marriage described cynically as a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Quiet about decent characters setting an example

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: setting the letters means arranging them anew, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the characters, i.e. letters, of the word decent

explanation.surface: Calm, respectable people serving as role models.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier case taken as a model, i.e. an example to follow.

clue.text: This should keep one in comfort to some degree

definitions.text: This should keep one in comfort to some degree

parts.words: This should keep one in comfort to some degree
parts.note: 'to some degree' looks like 'somewhat' but means at a set temperature, measured in degrees, by a device controlling heating

explanation.surface: A modest promise of reasonable comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat regulates heating to hold a room at a chosen temperature in degrees, keeping occupants comfortable.

clue.text: To create a disturbance could mean jail!

definitions.meaning: to cause trouble or commotion, as in stirring things up
slang for prison, as in 'doing time in the clink'

explanation.surface: Causing trouble could land you in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir means to agitate or cause commotion, and is also British slang for prison.

clue.text: Together many different noises can generate cacophony

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, i.e. many

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of varied sounds together make a horrible din.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissonance is a harsh clash of sounds, which is what cacophony means.

clue.text: This country dweller, let loose, is apt to snap

parts.note: in a British paper, a dweller in this country is a Brit

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rural resident who, once unleashed, is short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country dweller' suggests a rustic, but 'This country' means Britain, the newspaper's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brittle is hard but fragile, liable to snap or break easily.

clue.text: Support the boards — but behind the scenes

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the boards is a theatrical term for the stage

explanation.surface: Helping the theatre without appearing in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage means in the area behind a theatre's stage, or figuratively out of public view.

clue.text: Reduction in capital growth

parts.note: reads as a finance term, a fall in investment growth, but capital also means head, so it is a trim of what grows on one's head

explanation.surface: A financial report on falling investment returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut cuts back the growth on one's head; in finance it is also a reduction in an asset's value.

clue.text: Quite pleased about batting being moderate

indicators.note: one piece is placed about, round, the other

parts.note: content means satisfied, quite pleased
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricketer's mild satisfaction at being at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means exercising self-restraint, i.e. temperate or moderate.

clue.text: Cigar a man in credit reflected over

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: too means over, as in overmuch

explanation.surface: A man with a cigar, financially in the black, reflects on things.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: Dance couple's mounting pique

parts.note: a couple is two, so couple's gives two's

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means going up, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a pet is a fit of pique, a sulk

explanation.surface: A pair of dancers whose irritation is growing.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in march or polka time.

clue.text: Gaming houses that are equally popular in a Greek island

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
as means equally, as in as big
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Gambling halls that are a hit on a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Casinos are establishments for gambling, i.e. gaming houses.

clue.text: Animal refuge that is about right for a certain group

indicators.note: the outer pieces go about, around, the inner letter

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for birds or animals, as in dovecote
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sanctuary for animals that serves a select band of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people, a certain group.

clue.text: Oils requiring special treatment for storage

indicators.note: the letters need to be specially handled, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Oils must be handled with care when kept in store.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit used for storing grain or fodder.

clue.text: Turner, the bilingual

parts.note: la is the French for the
the in English, so the word given in two languages

explanation.surface: The painter Turner described as speaking two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it is a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that turns a workpiece to shape it, so it is literally a turner.

clue.text: Indicating the wine is running out?

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
something running out is ending

explanation.surface: A host warning that the port is nearly gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Portending means foreshadowing or signalling, i.e. indicating what is to come.

clue.text: Stay around a good man with the wind up

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a guy is a rope or stay that steadies a tent or mast
St, for saint, is a crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A frightened man is told to stay put by a good man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the wind up' looks like the idiom for scared, but it means with the wind rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty means marked by strong bursts of wind, so the wind is up.

clue.text: Not straight, so against entering means

indicators.note: one piece enters, goes inside, the other

parts.note: a way is a means or method
v is the abbreviation for versus, against

explanation.surface: Being crooked, as opposed to entering by proper means.
explanation.definitionFit: Wavy describes a line with curves, one that is not straight.

clue.text: What draws people at agricultural machinery shows

parts.note: a tractor is a farm machine

explanation.surface: Big farm vehicles are the crowd-puller at country shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractor is anything that attracts, i.e. draws people in.

clue.text: Wants to be seen returning about five hundred

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about, round, the letter
returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone wishing to be noticed when coming back with 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs as a noun or verb means requirements or wants.

clue.text: Offering a girl transport, that's all

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a form of transport

explanation.surface: Giving a young woman a lift is all one does.
explanation.definitionFit: Every means each one without exception, i.e. all.

clue.text: Soon chafe at having to go in to work

indicators.note: one piece has to go inside the other

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
to chafe at something is to resent it

explanation.surface: Someone irritated about having to go in to work soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently means in a short while, i.e. soon.
